documents.title: City hall moves to a four-day opening week
documents.text:
Residents of Brenton who need to renew a permit or register a business will find the town hall closed on Fridays from next month. The council voted by a narrow margin on Tuesday to open its public counters only from Monday to Thursday, extending the daily hours to 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. so that the weekly total remains almost unchanged. Staff will use Fridays for work that does not involve the public, such as processing applications and training.

Supporters of the change, led by council member Hannah Doyle, say it reflects the reality that most transactions are now done online. Last year, only a fifth of requests were handled at the counter, and Friday was the quietest day of the week. The saving, estimated at 140,000 dollars a year in energy and cleaning costs, will be used to improve the town's Web portal, which many residents find hard to navigate.

Critics warn that the plan favors the digitally skilled. Councilor Reggie Fontaine, who voted against, argued that older residents and newcomers with limited English rely on face-to-face help. "A town hall should serve the people who need it most, not the people who are easiest to serve," he said. In response, the council has promised that a telephone helpline will remain open on Fridays and that mobile advisers will visit the library once a month. The new arrangement will be reviewed after six months.

A dispute between councilors about their own salaries
questions.explanation: The council voted to close its public counters on Fridays, while extending hours on other days.

documents.title: Interview feedback
documents.text:
To: Lucia Fernandes
From: Martin Boyle, Recruitment, Aster Pharma
Subject: Your interview on 14 October

Dear Lucia,

Thank you for taking the time to meet our team on Tuesday. It was a pleasure to learn about your career, and I wanted to give you some feedback while the discussion is fresh. The panel was impressed by your knowledge of regulatory procedures and by the clear way you described the clinical trial you managed in Seville. Your answers on teamwork were convincing, and several members commented on your calm approach.

There were, however, two points of concern. First, the role involves frequent presentations to senior executives, and the panel felt that your answer to the question on how you would explain a delay to a board was somewhat vague. Second, they noted that you have less experience of budgeting than other candidates, a skill that is important for the post.

Despite these reservations, the panel would like to take you to the next stage, which is a presentation to the Director of Operations on 28 October. You would have fifteen minutes to propose how you would organize a trial in a new country, followed by questions. Please confirm whether the date is convenient by Friday, and let me know if you require any equipment.

Kind regards,
Martin Boyle

documents.title: Review: "The Cartographer's Daughter" (novel)
documents.text:
Rating: 4 out of 5

Elise Marchand's third novel opens on a promising note. In 1912, a young woman inherits her father's map shop in Antwerp and discovers among his papers a chart of an island that appears in no atlas. The first hundred pages, in which she follows the clues through archives and harbors, are as absorbing as any detective story, and Marchand's evocation of the port city is vivid without being decorative.

The middle section is less secure. A romantic subplot involving a ship's engineer is introduced with some haste and seems designed mainly to provide an excuse for a voyage. The prose, so carefully controlled earlier, loosens, and there are passages of dialogue that sound more like explanations to the reader than conversation between characters. Readers who prefer pace may feel the book lose its way.

The final chapters, however, redeem much of this. The island, when it finally appears, is neither a treasure nor a trick but something more unsettling, and the heroine's reaction to it provides the novel with a quietly moving ending. It is not a flawless book, but it is an intelligent and ambitious one, and it confirms Marchand as one of the more interesting historical novelists writing today.

choices: The book is a complete literary failure

questions.explanation: The reviewer criticizes the middle but calls the novel intelligent, ambitious and moving.

documents.title: Notice: Annual general meeting of the Linden Cooperative
documents.text: The annual general meeting of the Linden Housing Cooperative will take place on Saturday 18 October at 10:00 a.m. in the Parish Hall. All members are invited to attend and vote. The agenda includes approval of the accounts, the election of two board members, and a proposal to increase monthly charges by 4 percent to fund the replacement of the building's boiler. Members who cannot attend may give a proxy vote to another member using the attached form, which must be returned to the secretary by 10 October. Nominations for the board must be submitted in writing by 3 October. Lunch will be served after the meeting.

documents.title: Question about proxy voting
documents.text:
Dear Secretary,

I will be traveling on 18 October and would like to vote by proxy. I own a flat in the cooperative but my sister, who lives in the same building and is also a member, is willing to vote for me. I would also like to stand for election to the board; is it too late? Finally, I am against the increase in monthly charges, although I would support the boiler replacement if it were financed in another way, such as by a loan. Can this be put to the meeting?

Regards,
Hugo Marchetti

documents.title: Re: Question about proxy voting
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Marchetti,

Your sister may vote for you, provided that you complete the form and she signs it too. The deadline for returning it is 10 October. Unfortunately, nominations closed on 3 October, so you cannot stand this year. However, you can propose an amendment: any member may submit an alternative proposal in writing to the board by 12 October, and it will be added to the agenda if it is supported by five members. If you want to speak about a loan, I suggest you ask four others to sign the proposal.

Please note that a proxy holder may carry a maximum of two votes.

Kind regards,
Ofelia Brandt, Secretary

choices: To complain about the cost of holding the meeting
To ask how he can take part while he is away
To resign his membership of the cooperative
To report a fault in the building's boiler
questions.explanation: He asks about proxy voting, standing for election and proposing an alternative.

questions.explanation: A written proposal by 12 October must be supported by five members, that is himself and four others.

documents.title: Invoice 4420: Clearwater Cleaning Services
documents.text:
Client: Hollis & Grant Dental Clinic · Period: 1 to 31 March
Weekly office cleaning (4 weeks at 190 dollars): 760.00
Deep clean of treatment rooms (2 sessions at 240 dollars): 480.00
Window cleaning, exterior (1 visit): 150.00
Supplies surcharge (5 percent of cleaning charges): 62.00
Subtotal: 1,452.00 · Tax (6 percent): 87.12 · Total due: 1,539.12
Please pay within 30 days. Complaints about work must be made within five days of the service date.

documents.title: Complaint about service
documents.text:
Dear Clearwater,

We have received your invoice for March. Before we pay, I wish to raise two issues. First, the deep clean of the treatment rooms was scheduled for two sessions, but the cleaners came only once, on 14 March; on 28 March, nobody came, and no one from your office contacted us. Second, the invoice lists exterior window cleaning, but this was not requested. I would like to know why this was added.

Regards,
Dr. Neil Hollis

documents.title: Re: Complaint about service
documents.text:
Dear Dr. Hollis,

Thank you for telling us. I have confirmed that the session on 28 March was missed because of staff illness, and I apologize that we did not inform you. The charge for that session, 240 dollars, will be removed. The window cleaning was added on 20 March following a phone call from your receptionist, as our notes show, but I can remove this too if it was not authorized; please confirm.

I attach a revised invoice. Please note that the supplies surcharge will be recalculated on the revised total.

As a gesture of goodwill, we would also like to offer you a free deep clean of one treatment room next month, to be scheduled at a time that suits your team. We recognize that a dental clinic has high standards of hygiene, and we are reviewing our procedure so that a missed visit is always reported to the client on the same day.

Sincerely,
Dena Ruiz, Account Manager

questions.prompt: What problem does Dr. Hollis raise first?
choices: A cleaning session did not take place
The invoice was sent too late
The cleaners broke some equipment
The prices were higher than agreed
questions.explanation: Nobody came on 28 March for the second deep clean.

questions.prompt: How does the company explain the window cleaning?

questions.explanation: The charge for the session on 28 March, 240 dollars, will be removed.

questions.explanation: The surcharge is 5 percent of cleaning charges only: 760 + 480 = 1,240 gave 62. Removing the 240-dollar session leaves 1,000, so 5 percent is 50 dollars.

choices: Proof that he has already paid the invoice
A letter from his receptionist about the call
A new request for another window cleaning visit
Written confirmation that the job was not approved
questions.explanation: Ms. Ruiz asks him to confirm that the window cleaning was not authorized.
